solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One taking pleasure from attack on Georgia lawman?

indicators.note: in an across answer, 'attack on' the others means it is placed after them

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a DA is a district attorney, a US public prosecutor
a bout is a fit or attack of illness

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker gets a kick out of an assault on a sheriff in Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a restless person who flits from one social amusement to the next.

clue.text: Group's leader had dressed formally

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is G
had in the sense of possessed, owned

explanation.surface: The head of the band had put on evening wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowned means clad in a gown, the robe worn on formal or academic occasions.

clue.text: Head of state in Irish parliament to go off line

indicators.note: ER is placed inside DAIL

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the queen and head of state

explanation.surface: A president in the Dáil wanders off message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' looks like a first-letter pick, S; it is ER, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A train that derails leaves the track, so it goes off the rails.

clue.text: Marine fish, a food not fully digested in Hebridean isle

indicators.note: A and CUD are put inside BARRA

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides off Scotland
cud is food a ruminant brings back up to chew again

explanation.surface: A sea fish's meal, half digested, on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a predatory, sharp-toothed tropical sea fish.

clue.text: Drawing attention to consequence of batsman's poor form?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: emphasising, as by a line under words
second meaning: a batsman in poor form is ..., making too few runs

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as UNDER-SCORING, falling short of the runs expected in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Underscoring means emphasising, like underlining a point to stress it.

clue.text: Standard flash measurement used in astronomy

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
'in a flash' is in a second; SEC is short for second

explanation.surface: A unit of measure for a flash of light, apparently used by astronomers.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is a unit of stellar distance, about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: A minor charge for allotment

parts.note: a ward is a minor placed in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A small fee for a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor charge' looks like a small fee, but it is a child in care, a WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something allotted or granted, so it is an allotment.

clue.text: Irregular cops uneasy about organised raid

indicators.note: the rearranged cops go around the other letters
uneasy suggests restless jumbling of these letters
organised means put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Unconventional police are nervous about a planned raid.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: the scrambled police letters form the outer shell and the scrambled raid sits inside, with 'about' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals, now and then.

clue.text: Face fine when brewing stimulant

indicators.note: brewing means stewing or mixing up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: You look fine when making tea or coffee with its pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is the stimulating drug in coffee and tea.

clue.text: Catholic keeps backing Republican supporter, one joining in conflict

indicators.note: WIDE keeps the reversed letters held within it

parts.note: catholic in its lower-case sense means wide-ranging, broad

indicators.note: backing means the Republican supporter is read backwards

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A Catholic stands behind a Republican partisan who has joined a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' is not the Church here but the lower-case adjective meaning broad or all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: A war bride marries a serviceman during a war, so she joins him in the midst of the conflict.

clue.text: Refrain from song unavailable

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song
a dish that is off is no longer available

explanation.surface: A chorus from a song that can no longer be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a noun for a chorus, which fits 'song'; it is the verb meaning abstain.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay off something is an idiom for to stop doing or avoid it.

clue.text: Support at Covent Garden for Shaw's play?

definitions.text: Support at Covent Garden for Shaw's play?

parts.words: Support at Covent Garden for Shaw's play?
parts.note: Covent Garden was London's fruit market, where a cart holds apples; this is also the title of a Shaw play

explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is also the opera house district, so 'play' seems theatrical; the support is a fruit trader's barrow from the old market there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apple Cart is a 1928 political comedy by George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Musical quartet has worried about retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the combined letters are read in reverse
ATE goes around the four, holding it inside

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A four-piece group is anxious about withdrawing from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: AT(IV)E read backwards gives the answer; 'has' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Again water dry earth, ground close to hedge

indicators.note: ground means crushed or broken up, so the letters are rearranged
the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its last letter is E

explanation.surface: A gardener irrigates parched soil once more, the ground right by a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehydrate is to restore moisture, giving fresh water to something dried out.

clue.text: Lots of wives knocked down here?

definitions.text: Lots of wives knocked down here?

parts.words: Lots of wives knocked down here?
parts.note: in Cockney slang 'my old dutch' is a wife; lots at a sale are knocked down by the auctioneer

explanation.walkthrough: A Dutch auction starts high and drops the price; the clue jokes that the lots sold are 'dutches', wives in Cockney slang, knocked down by the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch auction is a sale in which the asking price is lowered until a bidder accepts.

clue.text: Crackling relating to small hole in humbug

indicators.note: RE and PIT go inside CANT

parts.note: cant is hypocritical talk, humbug
re means concerning, relating to
a pit is a small hollow or hole

explanation.surface: A crunchy sound about a little hole in a boiled sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humbug' suggests the British striped mint sweet, but here it is CANT, hypocrisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepitant describes something making a crackling or rattling noise.

clue.text: Doomed defendant brought about lawyer's end

indicators.note: brought about means placed around, so ACCUSED encloses the letter

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its last letter is R (ignoring the apostrophe-s)

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner caused the downfall of his own counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means under a curse, so fated to ruin.

clue.text: Broadcasting session unstarted after the speaker keeled over

indicators.note: the shortened sitting comes after the reversed ME
keeled over means turned upside down, so ME is reversed

parts.note: the speaker refers to himself as ME

indicators.note: unstarted means without its first letter

parts.note: a sitting is a session, as of a court or parliament

explanation.surface: A broadcast session ended early after the presenter collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer ME keeled over becomes EM, and SITTING without its start is ITTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Emitting means sending out signals or rays, as in broadcasting.

clue.text: Moving camera with metal casing fell over

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: copper is the metal, used for casing such as wiring and boilers

explanation.surface: A camera being shifted in its copper housing toppled over.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is an idiom for taking a heavy fall, originally from a horse.

clue.text: Exile elected to office rising in party

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside BASH

parts.note: a bash is a party

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a party voted in is IN

explanation.surface: A deported man, once voted into office, ascends within his party.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to send into exile, expelling someone from their country.

clue.text: Impassive detective much taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback means turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
lots means much

explanation.surface: A poker-faced detective is greatly surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means calm and unemotional, showing little feeling.

clue.text: Finished next, penning a note to increase demands

parts.note: time is up when it is finished

indicators.note: THEN pens, or encloses, the A

parts.note: then means next, afterwards
te is the seventh note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: Done, then onto the next thing, writing a note to ask for more.
explanation.definitionFit: To up the ante is an idiom from poker for raising the stakes or demands.

clue.text: Climbing record broken by unknown resident abroad

indicators.note: the reversed record is split by the X placed within
in a down answer climbing means going upward, so the record is read in reverse

parts.note: to tape is to record, and a tape is a record
X is the algebra symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: A climbing record broken by an unknown overseas mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat is an expatriate, someone living outside their native country.

clue.text: Unbecoming pressure on N America to sever relations

indicators.note: the letters cut IT in two, sitting between its letters

parts.note: IT is a coy word for sex, sexual relations

indicators.note: in an across answer, pressure placed on N America comes after it

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: It looks bad to apply pressure on North America to cut diplomatic ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' sounds diplomatic, but it is IT, a euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, so not becoming to the occasion.

clue.text: Mean devil entering lift

indicators.note: the devil goes inside SKY

parts.note: to sky a ball is to lift it high
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A wicked spirit gets into an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy portion is a stingy, meagre one.

clue.text: Illustrious companion, a pilot, runs off

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: off means removed, so the R is taken out

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a trial
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A distinguished friend who is an aviator dashes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' is not a flyer but a test, TRIAL; R for runs comes out to leave TIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatial means splendid and grand, like a palace, close to magnificent.

clue.text: Figures showing one ton in quarters

indicators.note: the I and T are placed inside DIGS

parts.note: digs are lodgings, living quarters
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Numbers showing a single ton of material in lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are the numerals 0 to 9, the figures used to write numbers.

clue.text: Worked on material, irritated after satirist cleared out

indicators.note: ITCHED follows the letters from satirist
the satirist is cleared of all inner letters, leaving its outside pair

parts.note: its first and last letters are S and T
itched means felt irritation

explanation.surface: A seamstress sewed, annoyed after a mocking writer left.
explanation.definitionFit: To stitch is to sew, working a needle and thread through fabric.
